The US defence secretary made the comments during a press conference this morning, a day after Thomas Massie, Kentucky’s Republican representative, introduced eight articles…

As we bring you the latest on the effort to impeach defense secretary Pete Hegseth, my colleague Anna Betts, has put together a primer about what to know about the push to oust Hegseth, and what happens next as we prepare for today’s key vote.

The question is absurd and the answer is: obviously not,” Vance said on social media. “Like so much of Congress, impeachment has become a…

On an episode of his podcast, Cruz said that it was “extremely likely, if not certain,” that the House will vote to impeach Hegseth.

Today, the House is poised to vote on a procedural motion on Pete Hegseth’s impeachment later today. As I flagged earlier, that means lower chamber lawmakers will vote on whether to refer Thomas Massie’s resolution to committee for further investigation, or table the measure entirely. If they don’t get enough votes (a…

Donald Trump is in Washington today. As of now, the president has no events open to the press on his schedule. While he’ll spend most of the day in closed-door meetings, he’ll take part in signing time at 3.30pm ET, and we’ll let you know if that opens up to reporters.

Following Pete Hegseth’s press conference, Donald Trump issued a brief, and glowing, assessment of his defense secretary’s performance, while blasting the Republican representative who is moving to impeach him. “Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defense against a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former…

One quick note – since Thomas Massie introduced his articles of impeachment on Monday, the House now has until Wednesday to take them up. The lower chamber can hold a vote on the House floor, decide to send the resolution to committee (for further investigation) or table the measure entirely. A vote could come as soon…
